title: A Stranger at the Gate
text: A man with a bag of tools and a dead son's name on his lips asks for a bed for the night. The rule of this house is that no one is turned from the gate.

choices.label: Give him a bed and bread
choices.chronicle: {When}, a stranger came to the gate and was given a bed and bread, as the rule of the house requires.

choices.label: Give him a bed only
choices.chronicle: {When}, a stranger slept in the guest room and left before Lauds, having been given what the house could spare.

title: Someone by the Wall
text: Someone has sat against the outer wall since dusk. He asks for nothing, only for the abbot. The gate is shut by the rule.

choices.label: Open the wicket and sit with him
choices.chronicle: {When}, the abbot sat with a stranger outside the wall until morning, against the rule of the house.

choices.label: Keep the gate shut
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gate stayed shut, and in the morning the man was gone from the wall.

yes.chronicle: {When}, pilgrims came to the grave of the saint with candles and gave what they had. The granary was the better for it.

no.chronicle: {When}, a few pilgrims came to the grave of the saint and went away again with little said.

effects.chronicle: {When}, in common prayer {monk} laid his anger down at the chapel door, and was seen to pick it up again only at the gate.
{When}, {monk} sang the Office with the others every night for a season, and at its end said he no longer needed to ask whether anyone heard it.
{When}, the scholars finished the autumn copying, and the scriptorium shelves were heavier by two books.
{When}, a letter came from the daughter house. The brothers there are well, and they asked for a copy of the Office.
